http_semantics.note: A request-side state error — querying a collection name that never existed or was just dropped — is answered HTTP 200 with a plain success body {"result":{"aliases":[]},"status":"ok"}; there is not even a business error code, the error branch is silently masked as success. Sibling faces on the SAME unknown name in the SAME script return real HTTP 404 (describe and count). Source forensics show the handler never performs collection-existence validation, so the 404 branch is unreachable on this path.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases -> actix get_collection_aliases -> do_list_collection_aliases (auth.check_collection_access only; no existence requirement) -> toc.collection_aliases -> alias_persistence.collection_aliases (scan alias map for entries whose target == name; empty Vec for unknown/dropped names) -> 200 CollectionsAliasesResponse{aliases: []}. No call to get_collection, resolve_name or validate_collection_exists anywhere in the chain, so StorageError::NotFound (-> HTTP 404) is unreachable on this endpoint. Sibling handlers (describe via do_get_collection -> toc.get_collection -> resolve_name -> validate_collection_exists; count likewise resolves the collection) raise NotFound for the same names -> 404 (observed). gRPC ListCollectionAliases (tonic) calls the same do_list_collection_aliases — identical behavior. Alias entries are cascade-removed on collection drop (collection_meta_ops.rs drop_collection -> alias_persistence.remove_collection), so no alias residue exists post-drop; only the missing existence check remains.

mundane_explanation.surviving: 200-with-empty-list on unknown/dropped collection for GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases persists under clean conditions: positive face on an existing collection returned exactly its 2 aliases (200), describe and count on the SAME never-created/dropped names returned 404 within the same script, names are fresh unique timestamps, sequence is single-threaded and deterministic. Source forensics show the handler chain contains no collection-existence validation while sibling handlers do (validation_absent). No by-design evidence: no code comment/docstring states an intentional 200-on-unknown for this endpoint, no doc statement promises it, and no repo test (tests/openapi/test_alias.py, jwt auth tests) documents it.
